operations.name: Create or update saved searches
operations.description:
Create or update multiple saved searches in a single request. This endpoint allows you to save up to 100 searches at once. When a search with the same name already exists in the target scope, the `duplicateStrategy` parameter controls the behavior: NEW_ONLY (default) skips duplicates, REPLACE overwrites existing searches, or APPEND_SUFFIX creates new searches with numeric suffixes (e.g., 'My Search (2)'). You can change the active scope using the `S1-Scope` header to manage SHARED searches in different scopes.

Note: A `teamToken` query parameter will be automatically added to each search URL if it is not already present. This token ensures the searches are scoped correctly.

responses.description: All searches were processed successfully. This includes searches that were saved, as well as searches that were skipped due to the duplicate strategy.
Partial success. Some searches were saved successfully, but others failed validation or encountered errors. Check the results array for details on each search.
Invalid request. The request body is malformed or contains invalid parameters.
Authentication required. Please provide valid credentials.
Permission denied. You do not have the required permissions to manage saved searches.
Internal server error. All searches failed to save due to a system error.

fields.description: How to handle searches with names that already exist in the target scope. NEW_ONLY (default) skips duplicates and marks them as SKIPPED in the response. REPLACE overwrites existing searches with the same name. APPEND_SUFFIX creates new searches by adding numeric suffixes like ' (2)', ' (3)' to duplicate names.
List of saved searches to create or update. Maximum 100 searches per request.
Individual result for each search in the request, in the same order as submitted.

operations.name: Delete saved searches
operations.description: Delete multiple saved searches in a single request. You can delete up to 100 searches at once by providing their names and types. Each search name must be unique within its type (PRIVATE or SHARED) and scope. Use the `S1-Scope` header to target SHARED searches in specific scopes.

responses.description: Partial success. Some searches were deleted successfully, but others were not found or encountered errors. Check the results array for details on each search.
Invalid request. The request body is malformed or contains invalid parameters.
Authentication required. Please provide valid credentials.
Permission denied. You do not have the required permissions to delete saved searches.
Internal server error. All searches failed to delete due to a system error.

fields.description: List of saved searches to delete, identified by name and type. Maximum 100 searches per request.
Individual result for each search in the request, in the same order as submitted.

operations.name: List saved searches
operations.description: Retrieves all saved searches visible to the current user. Saved searches allow you to persist and quickly access frequently used search queries in Event Search. Use the `type` parameter to filter by PRIVATE (user-specific) or SHARED (visible to all users in the scope) searches.

responses.description: List of saved searches retrieved successfully.
Forbidden. User does not have permission to manage searches.

query.name: type
query.description: Filter by search type. PRIVATE searches are visible only to you, while SHARED searches are visible to all users in your current scope. Defaults to PRIVATE if not specified.

fields.description: Zero-based position of the saved search in the list. This determines the display order.
Display name of the saved search. Must be unique within the same type and scope.
Visibility type. PRIVATE searches are visible only to you, while SHARED searches are visible to all users in the same scope. Use the S1-Scope header to manage searches in different scopes.
Event Search URL path with query parameters, typically starting with /events. This URL is used to navigate to the saved search.
